explain:
Each RTT the controller does three things: update an exact belief about the link, let a planner pick a mode, and, only when the mode leaves more than one move, run a depth-4 minimax search against a worst-case link. The behavior that comes out has the shape of BBR (start-up, cruise, probe up, drain for the min RTT), except every rate is set from a proven bound instead of an estimate.

  1. Keep a belief that never excludes the true link

    Every 7-observation window is checked against precomputed exact solutions of the link model (C, buffer B, bursts up to K, service up to one RTT late). Windows are intersected jointly in (C, B), and long runs of RTTs give a chained bound on C that removes the one-RTT ambiguity of a single window. Burstiness hypotheses K ∈ {1, 4, 16, 64} are ruled out by contradiction, and the smallest one is trusted after 20 informative RTTs (that confirmation is an assumption).

  2. Start-up: probe one BDP above the safe rate

    While max C is above 1.25 × min C the planner is in Explore. Here the search chooses among the largest rate no believed link would drop, holding the queue, and a probe one BDP above that rate. On every one of 805 searched RTTs we logged, the highest of these was optimal, and the search strictly preferred something else only once. Whatever the link delivers raises min C. With a buffer of at least a BDP this roughly doubles the rate every two RTTs. When the buffer is proven smaller than a BDP the budget falls to one packet every four RTTs, and growth becomes about one buffer per two RTTs. The queue is held under two BDPs throughout.

  3. Cruise at the proven capacity

    Once C is tight the controller sends min C, minus whatever the queue might exceed its provable floor by (about K + 1 packets). That gives at least 80% of the true C, and usually close to 100% because the chained bounds keep shrinking the interval. It leaves the queue near empty.

  4. Maintenance: probe, check for rises, drain

    Every 10 RTTs a one-RTT probe tests the buffer. Rise checks send 5/4 of max C for about 6 RTTs, 10, then 20, then 40 RTTs apart. They are the only way to see a rise, because a rise never contradicts the belief at the old rate. Each check costs about one BDP of queue (or loss when the buffer is under a BDP), and that cost is set by the model, not by the step size. Every 40 RTTs a drain empties the queue so the wrapper gets a min-RTT sample.

  5. Changes: restart at the longest consistent prefix

    When no link explains the history, the controller first asks whether a burstier K would. If not, the link changed: it finds the longest prefix some static link explains and restarts the belief right after it. Falls show up within a few RTTs, rises at the next rise check. For the 6 RTTs before a fresh window exists, it matches the delivery rate (Recover).
distilled:
A separate agent distilled the controller into rules that replace the search. On 3,850 logged RTTs (52 links: 45 used to check the rules and the 7 scenarios above, which were held out), the rules choose a minimax-optimal rate on every RTT. Run in the simulator, they reproduce every trace exactly at a tenth of the cost per step. There are no fitted thresholds. The rules are the planner restated, plus one sentence for the only place the search chooses.

What the distillation found

  • Two search bugs, now fixed by default. Beliefs deep in the lookahead could forget what their parent had proved, so they were broader than the parent's. And the adversary could answer with replies no unchanging link could produce. Each bug made the search undervalue a probe twice.
  • One choice the search makes for real reasons. On link n2 at RTT 68, probing now would fill the queue cap and force a hold next RTT. Holding now lets it probe next RTT instead. Both orders send the same amount, but the second ends the lookahead with a narrower worst-case range for C (14.7 against 20.8). It happened once in 805 searched RTTs.
  • The rules hand the decision to the search when probing would fill that cap. That happened on 32 RTTs, and the search sent the highest rate on 31 of them. The region was chosen from data, not proven, so new link sets should be rechecked with the search.
  • Exact trace equality needs ties broken toward the highest rate (--tie-high). With the default tie-break the search picks a lower, equally optimal rate at 9 of the 725 searched RTTs on the 45 links. Everything is at depth 4.
